title: Alien Alphabet Order
statement:
Recover a letter ordering from a dictionary sorted in an unknown alphabet.

Contract
- `words` is sorted in the lexicographic order of an unknown alphabet that uses only lowercase English letters. Each word is non-empty.
- Return a string containing exactly the distinct letters that appear in `words`, each once, in an order consistent with the word list. If several orders are consistent, return any of them.
- Words compare letter by letter; the first position where two words differ decides which comes first. A word that is a proper prefix of another must come first.
- Return an empty string if no order is consistent, including when a word is followed by one of its own proper prefixes. An empty word list returns an empty string.

Examples
- `{"zy", "zx", "yx"}` returns `"zyx"`.
- `{"abc", "ab"}` returns an empty string, because `ab` must precede `abc`.
- `{"dog"}` returns the letters d, o, g in any order.

examples.output: any arrangement of d, o, g

hints: Only the first differing position of two neighboring words tells you anything, and it tells you that one letter precedes another.
Turn each such fact into a directed edge between letters (remember letters that never get an edge), then find an order that respects every edge.

Use a topological sort; if it cannot place every letter there is a cycle, and a longer word directly before its own prefix is also invalid. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(1) space, where n is the total number of characters in all words (the alphabet is fixed at 26 letters).
inputSyntax: Input: words in sorted order separated by commas, using lowercase letters only, for example: zy,zx,yx
